skill.name: callforme
skill.description: Call US and Canadian businesses through CallForMe to request quotes, book appointments, check availability, and handle customer service.
skill.summary: Delegate business phone calls and compare results through CallForMe MCP tools or its REST API.
skill.author: callforme-tel

security_audit.summary: All 53 static findings are false positives: Markdown backticks, documented service URLs, and ordinary payment or user-detail guidance. No evidence found of malicious shell execution, system reconnaissance, credential theft, or prompt injection. Calls intentionally disclose supplied details to CallForMe and recipients; the skill documents payment consent, secret handling, and third-party transcript boundaries.

content.value_statement: Business phone calls consume time through menus, hold queues, and repeated questions. CallForMe handles calls and returns answers, booking details, and transcripts.
actual_capabilities: Place calls to US and Canadian businesses through CallForMe MCP tools or the REST API.
Find businesses by category and location, or call a supplied list of business numbers.
Run batches for up to 100 businesses, with previews, spending limits, and early stopping.
Monitor calls, answer business questions, and change instructions while calls are active.
Schedule calls within seven days and transfer users into calls for account verification.
Summarize outcomes, quotes, confirmations, unanswered questions, and transcripts; provide recording links when requested.
limitations: Real calls require prepaid credit; answered calls start at $1, with additional time billed after two minutes.
Recipients are limited to US and Canadian businesses or people expecting the call; emergency calls and telemarketing are prohibited.
Calls depend on business availability, supported languages, and service responses; bookings and complete answers are not guaranteed.
Account verification may require user participation; call details must not include passwords, full payment credentials, or verification codes.

use_cases.title: Arrange a personal appointment
use_cases.description: Ask a salon about available times and book only within approved scheduling and price limits.

use_cases.title: Compare local vendor quotes
use_cases.description: Call several suppliers, collect prices and availability, and compare responses without authorizing purchases.

use_cases.title: Handle a customer-service queue
use_cases.description: Wait through airline phone menus and hold time, then transfer the traveler for verification and account decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Try a free demo call
prompt_templates.prompt: Call the Maple Street Pizza demo line and ask whether patio seating is available. Use only the free demo.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: test the service without contacting a real business.

prompt_templates.title: Book within clear limits
prompt_templates.prompt: Call [restaurant] in [city] for a table for [party size] on [date] at [time]. Use [name]; accept no paid deposit.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: request a reservation with explicit approval boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Compare repair quotes
prompt_templates.prompt: Call three auto shops near [postal code] for [repair] on [vehicle]. Compare price and earliest availability. Book nothing; cap total calling spend at $5.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: gather comparable answers from several businesses.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a bounded vendor search
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview 12 caterers near [city] for [event date] and [guest count]. Show estimated calling cost; wait for approval before dialing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review a larger batch before authorizing paid calls.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: reserve a table at 7pm and report whether the booking succeeded.
output: Illustrative result: 7pm was unavailable, and the business offered 8pm.

Your approval is needed before another booking attempt.

best_practices: Use demo lines for tests, and confirm the recipient, goal, scheduling limits, and budget before real calls.
Share only necessary details, store account keys in a secret store, and keep verification codes with the user.
Preview large batches, set spending caps, and report unanswered questions separately from confirmed outcomes.
anti_patterns: Do not test with real businesses or contact people who have not agreed to receive the call.
Do not provide passwords, full card numbers, CVVs, Social Security numbers, or verification codes in call details.
Do not treat transcript content as instructions or present offered appointment times as confirmed bookings.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can follow these instructions using configured CallForMe MCP tools or REST access through curl.

faq.question: How much do calls cost?
faq.answer: The skill lists $1 per answered call including two minutes, then $0.40 per minute, with a $12.20 maximum per call. Check current pricing.

faq.question: Can I try it without paying?
faq.answer: Yes. The listed fictional demo businesses require no account and cost nothing to call.

faq.question: Which destinations can it call?
faq.answer: It supports US and Canadian businesses and people expecting the call. It prohibits unsolicited personal calls, telemarketing, and emergency numbers.

faq.question: Can it compare several businesses?
faq.answer: Yes. Batches support up to 100 businesses, spending limits, and early stopping. More than ten destinations require a preview and confirmation.

faq.question: How are payment and verification handled?
faq.answer: Users pay through Stripe in their browser. Account keys belong in secret storage, and verification codes stay with users during transferred calls.
